apps.localizedDescription: A free and open-source PlayStation 2 (PS2) emulator based on PCSX2, with native ARM64 JIT recompilers. Play PS2 games on your phone, PC, or gaming handheld.

versions.localizedDescription:
Automated nightly build for community testing (unsigned).

Every download is named `ARMSX2-nightly-DATE-COMMIT-PLATFORM`, so builds
from different nights stay distinguishable after you have downloaded them.

- macOS arm64: macOS-arm64.tar.xz
- Linux arm64: Linux-arm64-4K-pages.AppImage on most distros, or the 16K one on Asahi Linux and other Apple Silicon kernels (run getconf PAGESIZE if unsure)
- Windows arm64: Windows-arm64.zip
- RetroArch on Linux arm64: Linux-arm64-libretro-core.tar.zst, a 4K-page build
- Bare-display kmsdrm handhelds: Linux-arm64-SDL-handheld.tar.zst, a 4K-page build (Rocknix and Batocera run compositors, so use the Qt AppImage there instead)
- Android: Android-arm64.apk (installs as ARMSX2 Nightly, alongside the stable app)
- iOS: iOS-arm64.ipa, unsigned, sideload it (installs as ARMSX2 Nightly, alongside the stable app)

Coming from an old nightly? Nightlies are now a separate app, ARMSX2 Nightly, next to stable.

- Android: stable cannot install over an old nightly. Back up your saves and memory cards, uninstall the old nightly, then install the stable APK.
- iOS: your old nightly is the ARMSX2 iOS app and still has your saves. Copy them into ARMSX2 Nightly with the Files app.

## What's new
- GS: skip two results the CPU sprite road never reads
- GS: place the GS back thread next to the MTGS thread
- GS: end the front's space waits with a timeout, not a post per batch
- GS: sleep the front on a full ring or empty pool instead of yielding
- Android: the live settings apply keeps GS Multi-threading by its new name
- GS: mark the device in use as unknown without a renderer, and name the identified driver
- GS: list the vendor graphics libraries without scanning their contents
- armsx2-driverdiag: keep the tool out of the Android app build entirely
- GS: keep triangle names and mangled symbols out of the vendor-library version strings
- armsx2-driverdiag: the driver report as a command-line tool
- gsrunner: -take-gsdump writes a GS dump of the replay
- GS: write a driver report beside every GS dump
- GS/Vulkan: record whether the custom driver opened
- GS: drain the back thread before GSUpdateConfig replaces GSConfig
- GS: drain the back thread before a savestate load clears the device
- GS: drain the back thread between the front and back resets
- GS: record the palette load decision on the object that draws with it
- GS: GS multi-threading is on or off; remove the inline-records and lockstep modes
- GS: invalidate a palette's source memory on the object that reads it
- GS: carry TRXDIR in the back thread's move record
- GS/SW: a UV sprite's ramp bias is a hair, not a sixteenth
- GS/SW: the front end's texel rounding leaves a triangle that draws the console's plane
- GS/SW: cut the plane setup's cost in half
- GS/SW: the per-pixel reciprocal of Q on a fifteen-bit grid, rounded up
- GS/SW: a vertex with a negative Q is negated whole before the plane is built
- GS/SW: draw a perspective triangle with the console's S, T and Q planes
- GS/SW: the console's S, T and Q planes for a perspective triangle, as pure arithmetic
- gsrunner: a named ladder rung reads its own rectangle, not the cadence's
- gsrunner: checkpoints placed after a named packet, each reading its own region
- Pad nav: a modal's first focus that loads late still gets it
- LSFG: draw the overlay on generated frames, game image path always on
- Overlay: the LSFG line comes and goes with the performance overlay
- LSFG: generate from the game's own frame, not the finished screen
- LSFG: measure its own GPU time, on the overlay and in the log
- LSFG: motion measured at 432 lines, and FIFO when turned on in-game
- LSFG: automatic motion detail works, and a Half Precision switch
- Library music: ask for audio focus through one AudioManager
- Library music: Online Icons fades one track out, then the other in
- Library music: mix the tracks, then fade the old one out slowly
- Library music: a real fade back to the library
- Library music crossfades in and out of the Museum and Online Icons
- Online Icons: Shuffle works like the Icon Museum's, on Downloaded too
- Touch: P½ never puts a button back at full pressure for an instant
- Volume keys work in the shader editor, search and on-screen keyboard
- Online Icons: Shuffle on the All tab
- Icon Museum: with Shuffle on, every step is a new random icon
- Icon Museum: Shuffle stays put, and every step from there is random
- Icon Museum: Shuffle, and its buttons reach a controller
- Online Icons: Popular Today, the six most downloaded icons of the day
- Memory card covers: just "In the Icon Museum" on Discord
- Menu sounds: the select chime is now the short click
- Memory card covers: Discord and friends see the Icon Museum and Online Icons
- Memory card covers: Online Icons' selection stays put across a page turn
- Memory card covers: a click for Online Icons' page turns
- Volume keys work while a menu or prompt is open
- Volume keys work while a menu or prompt is open
- Memory card covers: names under covers, and a short MC Icon Info
- Memory card covers: music for the Icon Museum and Online Icons
- Memory card covers: Online Icons is a browser, one icon at a time
- Memory card covers: Online Icons, and a bookmark in the Icon Museum
- Memory card covers: publish every PS2IODB icon, zstd-compressed
- Memory card covers: a shorter MC Icon Info, with credits
- Memory card covers: drop the shared-save archive builder
- Memory card covers: build a serial-indexed icon set from PS2IODB
- Memory card covers: build an icon archive from shared saves
- Memory card covers: zero words in an icon texture are padding
- GS/Vulkan: trust a generation-2 Turnip build to order the declared loop on Adreno 7xx
- Memory card covers: the Icon viewer is now the Icon Museum
- Library Screen Saver: pause the library backdrop while it is up
- Library Screen Saver: drift on the icons' beat, not every refresh
- Memory card covers: moving icons drawn by the GPU
- LSFG: drop the Adreno 6xx overlay diagnostic
- Memory card covers: no calls in the pixel loop, bitmap copy off the UI thread
- Memory card covers: one beat for every moving icon, cheaper frames
- Memory card covers: search again where the search has improved; No spin faces front
- LSFG: keep shaders the cache can't hold, and say why generation is off
- Memory card covers: the screensaver is the Library Screen Saver
- Memory card covers: look inside CVM containers for disc icons
- Memory card covers: the Icon Viewer shows icons found on discs too
- Memory card covers: screensaver, Spin / No spin, lighter frames
- TEMP: LSFG diagnostic on the overlay for Adreno 6xx (#626)
- Memory card covers: icons from the game's own disc, ISO or CHD
- Memory card covers: every cover moves, seen from the console's height
- Memory card covers: bare icons, Icon Viewer, own menu section
- Memory Card Covers: the switch lives in the library's menu
- Memory Card Covers: the selected cover comes to life, and better still poses
- Library: Memory Card Covers, a game's PS2 save icon as its cover
- Touch: drop the #765 glide diagnostics
- Touch: D-pad directions obey the glide mode like buttons
- Touch: with multi-touch on, a thumb can glide on and off the D-pad
- Touch: a macro button lights up while it fires
- Multitap: a per-game setting stays with its game

- Drivers: the UBWC flag hint's description is not about one GPU

- Touch: multi-touch owns P½, macros and turbo like any button

- Drivers: Turnip options, with the UBWC flag hint
